text.p: -- J.P. Morgan said on Monday it had started coverage of Sweden's Nordbanken with a rating of market performer.

-- Analysts Catherine Woods and Haakon Boenes wrote in a report that Nordbanken was Sweden's fourth-largest bank and its most profitable. The Swedish government owns 59.4 percent of the bank and is committed to selling it off in full.
-- "We believe that the high profitability is driven by the large base of cheap salary and deposit accounts which funds a (60 billion crown) bond portfolio," they wrote.
-- "We expect a 10.5 total return over the next year ... and a 12-month target price of (200 crowns)."
-- Woods and Boenes added, "We believe that the Swedish banking sector is now fairly valued at current levels and thus do not expect any further upside from a sector re-rating."
-- The company's shares closed at 188 on Monday.
